list.name: pod
list.label: Pod
list.description: Applies only to the per-pod panels. Aggregate panels deliberately ignore it so pod churn does not gap the graphs.

panels.title: Documents by Outcome (rate)
panels.description:
- This dashboard covers the SIDECAR only: the hub image running as a native sidecar inside `applications-knowledge-service-be-go-*`, reached over loopback. It does every document this platform ingests.
- `succeeded` is the only outcome that wrote a document. `reused` short-circuited on same source_url + same checksum and cost one lock acquisition.
- Read `reused` as saved work, not throughput: leaving it in the same series as `succeeded` would make a redelivery storm look like a capacity increase.
- `cancelled` means the caller disconnected at a checkpoint — knowledge-service giving up, usually its own timeout.

panels.title: Ingest Duration — p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
- Admission to terminal outcome, per document.
- Shares a bucket ladder with `knowledge_service_pipeline_ingester_request_duration_seconds` on purpose. Compare them bucket-for-bucket: the GAP is queue and transport, not this service.
- `reused` documents land near zero and pull the p50 down, so read this with the outcome split beside it.

panels.title: Failure Error Codes (rate)
panels.description:
- The classification the caller was handed. Retryability is a property of the class, never of whether the client happened to disconnect.
- `db_unavailable` and `coordination_timeout` are retryable and self-correcting at low rates; a sustained rate means the coordinator pool is the ceiling.
- `malformed_content`, `checksum_mismatch` and `object_too_large` are terminal — retrying those burns the caller's delivery budget for nothing.

panels.title: Reuse & Success Share
panels.description:
- `reused` share rising is redelivery: the same document arriving again with an unchanged checksum. Cheap, but it means work upstream is being repeated.
- `succeeded` share falling while total rate holds is the shape that preceded the 2026-08-26 incident, when the ingester answered `success=false, retryable=false` at 60-550 docs/min and did no real work at all.

panels.title: In Flight vs Queued
panels.description:
- `in_flight` is bounded above by INGEST_MAX_CONCURRENT (10 deployed). `queued` is documents blocked on the admission semaphore.
- In flight pinned at the limit with nothing queued is a busy but healthy sidecar. A rising QUEUE is the point at which raising INGEST_MAX_CONCURRENT — and INGEST_COORDINATOR_POOL_MAX with it — is the remedy rather than more replicas.
- The two never overlap: a document is counted in exactly one of them.

panels.title: Admission Wait p95 by Result
panels.description:
- Waiting is deliberate backpressure, not an error: past the coordinator pool ceiling psycopg raises PoolError, which classifies as a RETRYABLE db_unavailable, so the caller re-sends and adds load to a system already at its limit. Blocking converts that into a queue.
- A `timeout` sample never touched a store — nothing retracted, no ledger row — so it is safe to retry immediately.
- The ladder starts at a 0 bucket so an uncontended admission is distinguishable from one that waited a tenth of a second.

panels.title: Document Lock Wait p95 by Result
panels.description:
- Do NOT read this as capacity. Waiting here means the SAME document is being ingested concurrently — usually a redelivery racing its own original — which is exactly what the per-document coordinator lease exists to serialize.
- Admission and this share ONE budget (INGEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS), so a queued request cannot spend the full budget twice.
- `error` means try_acquire itself raised: pool exhaustion or a lost connection, not contention.

panels.title: Ingest Duration Heatmap
panels.description: - The distribution the percentiles flatten. Two bands usually means two populations — `reused` short-circuits against real ingestions — rather than a bimodal latency problem.

panels.title: Failures by Mutation Phase (rate)
panels.description:
- The metric that says whether a failure was EXPENSIVE.
- `pre_mutation`, `acquire`, `acquire_timeout`, `admission_timeout` touched no store: the prior document is intact and a retry is free.
- `prior_retraction_started` / `new_writes_started` mean prior state was already deleted. The document was retrievable before the attempt and is not now — a retry has to rebuild it.
- `ledger_pending` means the new document is written and READY and only the bookkeeping failed.

panels.title: Rollbacks of Partial Writes (rate)
panels.description:
- Every sample is a document that was mutated and then cleaned up.
- `failed` rising is a dependency problem. `cancelled` rising is callers giving up on us mid-write — check knowledge-service's own timeout before assuming this side is at fault.

panels.title: Ledger Write Failures (rate)
panels.description:
- `op="success"` is the costly one: the document is fully written and READY but the ledger does not say so, so the caller is handed a retryable failure and the WHOLE document is re-ingested to reconcile one row.
- Non-zero here means real work is being redone. It is also invisible everywhere else — the ingestion looks like a failure to the caller and like a success in the stores.

panels.title: Destructive-Phase Failure Share
panels.description: - Share of failures that had already deleted prior state. This is the number to alert on rather than the raw failure rate: a service failing 5% pre-mutation is annoying, a service failing 5% mid-write is losing documents that used to be retrievable.

panels.title: Cached Object Size — p50 / p95
panels.description:
- `stored` is what S3 billed and transferred; `decoded` is what the rest of ingestion actually chews through.
- content-service zstd-compresses the text bucket unconditionally at 10-40x, so without the split the two populations would share one distribution and neither would read.
- A cluster of stored samples against 25 MiB is rejection pressure (INGEST_S3_MAX_OBJECT_BYTES), not a size distribution.

panels.title: Achieved Compression Ratio
panels.description:
- decoded bytes / stored bytes, aggregated. Expect roughly 10-40x on text.
- A ratio collapsing toward 1 means objects are arriving uncompressed — legacy objects with no `codec` metadata key, which is legal but means content-service wrote them by an older path.

panels.title: Cache Read p95 & Error Rate
panels.description:
- Covers the whole read: GET, streaming, checksum compare and zstd decode. Splitting further would need timers around code paths that mostly raise.
- `undecodable_content` at volume is the 2026-08-26 signature: a reader that does not dispatch on the `codec` user-metadata key gets raw zstd bytes and fails every object terminally.

panels.title: Document Bytes Handed to Processing
panels.description:
- `source="cached"` is the V2 path (decoded S3 text); `source="upload"` is a direct upload, which should not occur on the sidecar.
- **Read every stage duration against this.** A slow embedding stage on a 90 MiB document is arithmetic, not a regression.

panels.title: Stage Duration p95
panels.description:
- **Start here when ingestion is slow.** This breakdown exists nowhere else: the caller sees one streaming RPC whose progress frames carry a percentage, not a duration.
- Stages in pipeline order: `parse`, `ontology_infer`, `db_store`, `chunking`, `embedding`, `triple_extraction`, `kg_post`, `finalize`.
- `triple_extraction` normally dominates; descend into the Extraction row below to see whether that is the primary pass or the optional verify/discovery passes, which are the two that can be switched off.

panels.title: Stage Share of Wall Time
panels.description:
- Seconds of work per second, per stage — i.e. how much of the sidecar's concurrent capacity each stage is consuming right now.
- Unlike the p95 next door this is weighted by volume, so a slow stage that runs rarely stays small. It is the panel that answers "what would I optimise", where p95 answers "what is slow".
- The total across stages approximates documents in flight.

panels.title: Processing Duration p95 by Outcome
panels.description:
- DocumentProcessor only, excluding admission, lock and S3 fetch. The gap between this and Ingest Duration on the top row is everything the coordinator does.
- `error` far below `ready` is the healthy shape: failures should be cheap.

panels.title: Records / Chunks / Triples per Document
panels.description:
- What each document actually produced, p50 and p95.
- **A 0-chunk document is not retrievable.** In strict (V2) mode that is a terminal MalformedContentError, so a rise in the p50 sitting at 0 means content is arriving that we cannot chunk.
- Triples at 0 with chunks healthy means extraction found nothing — check the Extraction row rather than assuming failure.

panels.title: Documents In Processing vs Completion Rate
panels.description:
- Stall detection. A flat non-zero in-flight with a completion rate at zero is wedged, not busy — and every histogram goes quiet in that state, so nothing else shows it.
- In-flight is taken inside the per-filename lock, so documents blocked behind a same-filename upload are not counted here.

panels.title: Processing Outcomes (rate)
panels.description:
- `ready` vs `error` leaving DocumentProcessor. Counts documents, not attempts.
- Compare with Documents by Outcome at the top: a document can process to READY and still fail the ingestion at the ledger step.

panels.title: Vector Operation p95

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, operation, status) (rate(knowledge_hub_vector_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~".*knowledge-hub-be-go-sidecar", namespace="$namespace"}[5m])))

panels.description:
- `add_chunks` is the whole embed-and-write stage; `upsert` / `put_vectors` is the write alone, instrumented separately because the Pinecone and S3 Vectors stores LOG AND SWALLOW their write failures.
- That is why `status="error"` on the write operation matters more than it looks: `add_chunks` returns normally in that case and reports success.

panels.title: Chunks Written vs Chunks Produced
panels.description:
- **The silent-data-loss check.** `produced` is what chunking made; `written` is what the vector store acknowledged.
- These should track each other exactly. A persistent gap means writes are being dropped by the swallow described next door, and the documents involved are indexed as READY while being unsearchable.

panels.title: Embedding Batches (rate)
panels.description:
- The embedding stage is one long call from the outside. This is the only evidence a large document is ADVANCING through it rather than hanging.
- A flat rate with `embedding` rising on the stage p95 is a stalled embedding provider.

panels.title: Graph & Database Write p95
panels.description:
- Triple writes and the per-document record store. `add_triples` on Neptune fans out into many round trips; see the Neptune panel on the standalone Overview for the per-request view.
- `store_document` slow with a healthy `query` usually means the shared PostgreSQL is write-saturated by concurrent sidecars, not that this document is unusual.

panels.title: Extraction Phase p95
panels.description:
- The breakdown behind `stage="triple_extraction"`, which is usually the dominant stage.
- `pass1` is the primary guided/dynamic extraction. `pass2` (discovery), `verify` and `tabular` are optional passes — if they dominate, they are the levers.

panels.title: Model Calls by Status (rate)
panels.description:
- Extraction fires many short prompts per document, so this rate is roughly records-per-second, not documents-per-second.
- `error` includes a throttle that exhausted botocore's adaptive retries; a rise here with rising stage p95 is Bedrock quota, not model latency.

panels.title: Tokens per Second
panels.description: - Ingestion token spend. Multiply by the per-model rate for cost; the model label is what makes that computable from the series alone.

panels.title: Prompt Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description:
- Process-local cache keyed by sha256(model_id + prompt), 2048 entries, FIFO.
- Expected to be LOW: the same record rarely repeats within one ingestion. A high ratio means the corpus is repetitive; a ratio near zero is normal and not a fault.
- Note the cache is per pod, so it resets on every sidecar restart.
